components.css: .ds-quiz{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:10px;max-width:22rem;font-family:'Figtree Variable', 'Noto Sans Arabic Variable', ui-sans-serif, system-ui, sans-serif;} .ds-opt{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;gap:12px;min-height:56px;width:100%;padding:12px 16px;border:0;border-radius:0.5rem;background:var(--paper-raised);color:var(--ink);box-shadow:0 1px 2px var(--shadow-ink), 0 12px 32px -12px var(--shadow-ink);font-size:0.875rem;text-align:left;cursor:pointer;transition:all 200ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1);} .ds-opt:hover{background:color-mix(in oklch, var(--paper-sunk) 70%, var(--paper-raised));} .ds-opt:active{transform:scale(0.99);} .ds-opt:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--accent);outline-offset:3px;} .ds-opt.is-correct{background:var(--good-wash);color:var(--good);font-weight:600;box-shadow:0 0 0 2px var(--good);} .ds-opt.is-wrong{background:var(--again-wash);color:var(--again);font-weight:600;box-shadow:0 0 0 2px var(--again);} .ds-opt.is-dim{opacity:0.7;color:var(--ink-faint);box-shadow:none;}

narrative.overview:
Arabisa should feel like a well-kept study notebook lying open next to the Madinah book. It uses warm manuscript paper, deep indigo ink, and a single saffron mark where the learner's attention belongs. The mood is calm, warm, and unhurried. Arabic script is the hero of every screen. The interface around it (headers, labels, navigation, stats) stays quiet and compact, so a five-minute session on the phone feels focused rather than busy.

The system is a single portrait column, at most 36rem wide, made of softly lifted paper cards on a paper ground. Hierarchy comes from tone rather than chrome. The page is the paper, cards are a sheet raised above it, and wells such as icon tiles, progress tracks, and inactive pills are pressed slightly into it. Saffron is used sparingly: the brand mark, the active tab, "new" and "continue" badges, focus rings, and in-progress state. The strongest action on a screen is always solid ink on paper, never a saffron fill.

Dark mode ("Dark Ink") is not an inverted light theme. The paper becomes deep indigo night, the ink becomes warm parchment, and saffron brightens into lamplight. It is built for learners studying after Isya.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper and indigo ink, in OKLCH, with a full light and dark pair for every role.
One accent (saffron), plus two semantic inks for learning state: mint for correct or mastered, brick for wrong or "again".
Figtree for the interface and Noto Sans Arabic for Arabic, with Arabic always set larger and with more line height.
Softly lifted cards with an ambient shadow tinted by the ink colour. Never hard drop shadows.
Modest radii (4–12px), a gentle press-scale on tap, and one expo-out ease for everything that moves.

rules.name: The One Mark Rule
rules.body: Saffron is a mark, not a surface. It appears as small fills, washes, text, and outlines. No saffron-filled buttons, banners, or full cards.

rules.name: The Ink Leads Rule
rules.body: The single most important action on a screen is a solid ink button with paper text (`button-primary`). Saffron draws attention to state. Ink drives action.

rules.name: The Learning-State Rule
rules.body: Mint and brick mean exactly two things: right/mastered and wrong/again. Never use them for decoration, categories, or branding.

rules.name: The Paired Theme Rule
rules.body: Every new colour token ships with both a light and a dark value, defined in all three blocks of `layout.css`: `:root`, `[data-theme='dark']`, and the `prefers-color-scheme` fallback.

rules.name: The Harakat Room Rule
rules.body: Every Arabic run carries `lang="ar"` and `dir="rtl"`, which applies the Arabic font and line-height 1.7. Never set Arabic below 1.125rem, and never tighten its line height. Diacritics must never clip.

rules.name: The Arabic Is Bigger Rule
rules.body: Whenever Arabic and Indonesian appear together, the Arabic is larger. Transliteration sits between them in italic Saffron Ink.

rules.name: The Tabular Count Rule
rules.body: Streaks, scores, and counts use `tabular-nums` so they don't jitter as they change.

rules.name: The Warm Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are always tinted by `--shadow-ink`, never neutral black or grey, and always soft and wide. No hard offsets and no coloured glows.

rules.name: The Two Heights Rule
rules.body: There are only two elevations: Card at rest and Lift for floating or hovered elements. Don't invent a third.

dos: Do use the semantic tokens (`paper`, `paper-raised`, `paper-sunk`, `line`, `ink`, `ink-soft`, `ink-faint`, `accent`, `accent-ink`, `accent-wash`, `good`, `again`) through their Tailwind utilities. Never hard-code colours.
Do wrap every Arabic run in `lang="ar" dir="rtl"`, and keep it larger than the Indonesian beside it.
Do make the main action a full-width, 48px ink button, and give every tappable element a press-scale between 0.96 and 0.99.
Do use `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` (`ease-out-expo`) for movement, with durations of 200–300ms for UI and up to 700ms for progress and flips.
Do give every animation a `prefers-reduced-motion` fallback (a cross-fade or nothing at all).
Do keep content inside the centred 36rem column and clear the bottom nav with 96px of bottom padding.
donts: Don't fill buttons, banners, or cards with saffron. It is a mark, not a surface.
Don't use mint or brick for anything except right/mastered and wrong/again.
Don't use neutral grey or black shadows, hard offsets, or a third elevation level.
Don't use radii above 12px on containers, or pill-shaped buttons.
Don't shrink Arabic below 1.125rem or tighten its line height below 1.7.
Don't add a colour token without its dark-mode pair.
